introSk: Westminster is the classic first-time London base: Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament, Buckingham Palace, Trafalgar Square and the West End theatres are all within walking distance.
Soho and Covent Garden suit couples and night owls, Marylebone and Mayfair are quieter and smarter, and Paddington and Victoria are handy for Heathrow and Gatwick trains.

Soho and Covent Garden suit couples and night owls, Marylebone and Mayfair are quieter and smarter, and Paddington and Victoria are handy for Heathrow and Gatwick trains.

introSk: Kensington and Chelsea combine white stucco terraces, garden squares and three of the city's free museums – the Natural History, Science and V&A – around Exhibition Road.
Notting Hill brings Portobello Road market and pastel houses, Knightsbridge has Harrods and Hyde Park on the doorstep, and Earls Court offers better-value flats on the Piccadilly line.

introSk: Camden mixes markets, live music and Regent's Canal towpaths, while King's Cross and St Pancras are the gateway for Eurostar and trains to the north.
Bloomsbury puts the British Museum and leafy squares close by; Hampstead and Primrose Hill give village calm with views across the skyline from the Heath.

introSk: The Square Mile is London's financial heart – St Paul's Cathedral, the Gherkin and the Tower of London – and is quiet and good value at weekends.
Next door, Shoreditch, Spitalfields and Hackney are known for street art, independent shops, food markets and some of the city's best bars.

introSk: The South Bank riverside runs from the London Eye past the National Theatre, Tate Modern and Shakespeare's Globe to Borough Market and Tower Bridge.
London Bridge and Bermondsey suit food lovers, Waterloo is central and well connected, and Battersea, Clapham and Brixton offer larger flats and lively local high streets.

introSk: Greenwich is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the Royal Observatory, the Cutty Sark and wide parkland views back across the Thames to Canary Wharf.
Canary Wharf and the Isle of Dogs offer modern apartments on the Elizabeth and Jubilee lines, and riverboats make the trip into central London part of the holiday.

introSk: Richmond, Kew and Twickenham feel like a riverside market town inside London, with Richmond Park's deer, Kew Gardens and towpath walks along the Thames.
Wimbledon, Putney and Chiswick suit families and longer stays, with quieter streets, good schools and fast trains back to Waterloo.
